news.title: Amputee World Cup: Ghana win first title, beat Morocco 1-0
news.lede: Ghana won the Amputee World Cup for the first time on Sunday night, beating Morocco 1-0 in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, with a goal from captain Richard Opentil in the 32nd minute. The win makes Ghana’s Black Challenge the second African side to be crowned world champions in amputee football, after Angola in 2018, and settles the first all-African final in the tournament’s history in their favour. The final at the San Martin stadium kicked off at 19:30 local time on Sunday, 01:30 GMT on Monday. Opentil’s shot took a deflection off a Moroccan defender early in the second half (amputee football is played in halves of 25 minutes), and Ghana defended the lead for the rest of the match, the Ghana Football Association said.

news.title: 2031 Women's World Cup Confirmed to Be Co-Hosted by 4 Countries Including US; UK for 2035
news.lede: ▲ FIFA The 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup will be co-hosted by four North and Central American countries: the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica, and Jamaica. It has been confirmed that the 2035 tournament will be held in the United Kingdom. Major foreign media outlets, including AP and AFP, reported that FIFA finalized the host locations for both tournaments during an extraordinary congress held virtually on the 23rd (local time). Both bidding proposals were sole candidates and were passed by acclamation without a vote.

news.title: Ghana win the amputee World Cup, two days after sorting out their players' bonuses
news.lede: Ghana’s amputee football team won the World Cup in Mexico on Sunday, two days after a mining company, the national football association and the Paralympic committee agreed to cover bonuses and daily allowances the players were still owed when they reached the semifinals, according to Ghanaian broadcaster 3News. Under that Nov. 20 agreement, Gold Fields Ghana would bring forward part of its 2027 sponsorship, drawn from a two-year, $5 million deal signed with the Ghana Football Association in May. The money would pay each player and delegation member $8,000 if Ghana reached the final, a figure for approved allowances and bonuses rather than prize money, the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana said, according to 3News and MyJoyOnline.

news.title: Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir
news.lede: Caroline Weir says it is "amazing" that Scotland will host the World Cup finals. Scotland captain Caroline Weir says hosting the 2035 Women's World Cup along with England, Northern Ireland and Wales will usher in "an amazing decade of excitement" for the game in her homeland. World governing body Fifa confirmed on Monday that the United Kingdom will host a football World Cup for the first time since England won the men's tournament on home soil in 1966. Scotland's national stadium at Hampden Park in Glasgow and Hibernian's Easter Road Stadium in Leith are among 19 venues chosen for the 39-day competition involving 48 teams.

news.title: FIFA Names USA, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica Hosts of 2031 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: The United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will jointly host the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup, while the United Kingdom’s four football associations have been selected to stage the 2035 edition. FIFA has officially appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts of the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup, which will make history as the first edition of the tournament to feature 48 participating teams. The announcement was made during FIFA’s Extraordinary Congress held virtually, where member associations approved the host nations by acclamation following comprehensive bidding processes. The 2031 tournament will also mark the first time the FIFA Women’s World Cup is staged across four different member associations, representing a significant milestone in the global development of women’s football.
